edits.before: 胡适自己对来龙去脉的解释是反对单因论。他开玩笑说，历史上的意外事件往往比“单因”——经济、色欲、上帝之类——更重要：正因为这些单因对所有事件皆可解释，它们也就不可解释任何事件。就他这段经历而言，传单、送别诗、湖上险些翻船都是意外；他把一连串小意外看作推力，这是他本人的史观，不是本文的结论。

edits.before: Hu's own explanation of how it all happened is that he opposed single-cause theories of history. He used to joke that accidents matter more than any monistic cause — economics, lust, God and the rest: those single causes explain everything that has ever happened, and precisely because they explain everything, they explain nothing. In his own story the leaflet, the farewell poem and the near-capsize on the lake were accidents. Reading a chain of small accidents as the push behind his position is Hu's own view of history, not a finding of this article.
edits.after: Hu's own explanation of how it all happened is that he opposed single-cause theories of history. In this episode he explicitly called the farewell poem a small accident, and said that a chain of small accidents had gradually forced him into his position; placing the leaflet and the dispute that followed the near-capsize on the lake in that chain is this article's own grouping. Reading a chain of small accidents as the push behind his position is Hu's own view of history, not a finding of this article.

edits.before: Two days later, another accident. On July 8 Ren Hongjun, Chen Hengzhe of Vassar, Mei Guangdi, Yang Quan, Tang Yue and others were rowing on Cayuga Lake when a black cloud gathered overhead, a storm broke and the rain fell; pulling for shore in a hurry they nearly capsized, and all came away soaked and dishevelled. For that band of Chinese students it was a real adventure, and Ren wrote it up in Fanhu jishi (Boating on the Lake), an old four-character-style poem he mailed to Hu for criticism. It used archaic words such as the particle yan, of the kind found in the Book of Songs — Hu had earlier written an essay on that very word — and he disliked dead diction mixed with modern language. He wrote back that the poem was bad because its wording was thoroughly incongruous, and he spoke of dead language of three thousand years ago (both paraphrased from the Chinese). Ren was indignant. More interesting was the letter that followed: Mei, his other friend at Harvard, riding to the rescue in high dudgeon. Under the influence of his conservative teacher Babbitt, Mei opposed all of Hu's radicalism to the end — language becomes poetic only after first-rate poets refine it, and the language of literature, poetry above all, must be beautified by first-rate poets and artists before it counts as poetic diction. On that ground he lashed Hu's ideas.

edits.before: It appeared in New Youth in January 1917 and stirred a great response. Two Peking University professors took it seriously. Chen Duxiu, an unbending revolutionary, answered with "On Literary Revolution," publicly backing a literary revolution and saying frankly that the banner had been raised by his friend Hu Shi; he was only hoisting a flag in support. Qian Xuantong, professor of classical phonology, a master of ancient prose and a disciple of the great scholar Zhang Taiyan, wrote no article but sent Chen and Hu long letters — small criticisms, great praise — also printed in New Youth; that so eminent a classicist should sympathize buoyed their cause. Zhao Yuanren often said that Hu's vernacular poems and essays were "not vernacular enough," not the genuine spoken style ordinary people used. Hu admitted it: like a woman who had bound her feet for forty, or even twenty, years, however much she loosened the bindings she would never recover natural feet.

edits.before: 作者推断：他选择以身作则，并不只是姿态，而是把分歧改造成可检验的问题。“白话不能用之于诗”是个全称判断，理论上一首像样的白话诗就能动摇它；反之，没有诗，再多书信也只是意见相持。他把新诗集提前定名《尝试集》，等于当众揽下举证责任，把胜负交给一场公开、长期、别人看得见的试验。一种解释是，这也呼应了译注者唐德刚对他的定位——夹在必然与偶然之间的“实验主义者”，不肯听任事情自然演变，而要在试验中寻找方向。不过「没有“胡适”，恐怕也就没有“白话文运动”——至少运动也不会在那时就发生了」是唐德刚的评论，不是可核实的史实。

edits.before: The author's inference: his decision to lead by example was not merely a pose; it converted a disagreement into a testable question. The claim that the vernacular cannot be used for poetry is a universal one, and one decent vernacular poem is enough in principle to shake it; without a poem, letters could go on forever as a standoff of opinions. By naming the collection Experiments in advance, he publicly took on the burden of proof and left the outcome to a long, open trial that others could watch. One reading is that this matches the translator-editor Tang Degang's portrait of him as a pragmatist standing between necessity and chance, unwilling to let events drift and determined to search out the right direction through experiment. Still, Tang's remark — in paraphrase, that without Hu Shi there would probably have been no Vernacular Movement, or at least it would not have happened then — is commentary, not verifiable history.

edits.after: 1915到1917年，一个自称保守、认为语言文字最不易变的中国留学生，按他自述，是被几首打油诗和朋友的反对，一步步推到只用白话作诗的决定上；更早，一张传单让他起意在文字改革上尽点力。他把主张写得温和，《新青年》主编陈独秀却替他把旗子举高成“革命”。

edits.before: Between 1915 and 1917, a Chinese student in America who called himself a conservative — who thought language and writing the world's most unchanging things — was, by his own account, pushed by a leaflet, a few doggerel verses and his friends' opposition into writing poetry in the spoken language alone. He worded his claim modestly; Chen Duxiu, editor of New Youth, raised the banner for him, into "revolution."

He worded his claim modestly; Chen Duxiu, editor of New Youth, raised the banner for him, into "revolution."

issues.problem: dek 用“按他自述”把传单与打油诗、朋友反对并列，说成是它们一起把他推到只用白话作诗的决定上。analysis.0 却明确说“把传单……也放进这一串，这是本文的归并”。两处说法互相矛盾。证据中，胡适只说传单让他懊悔，进而去研究文字问题（HS-E5）。他点名为“意外”的是送别诗；HS-E9 的“这些事件”具体指哪些，从摘录看不出。

evidence.quote: 我作诗送我的朋友梅光迪去哈佛这一件意外的小事
一连串的小意外事件，逐渐地强迫我采取了这个立场
并想在〔文字改革〕这方面尽点力

issues.proposed: dek 改为“……按他自述，是几首打油诗和朋友的反对，一步步把他推到只用白话作诗的决定上；更早，一张传单让他开始认真研究文字问题。”英文同步改为“…was, by his own account, pushed by a few doggerel verses and his friends' opposition into writing poetry in the spoken language alone; earlier, a leaflet had first set him studying the question of writing.”

issues.problem: “梅光迪说的范围更宽”（英文 drew the line more widely）有歧义。按证据，梅光迪允许白话使用的范围其实更窄（把高级散文也排除在外），读者可能读成他更宽容。

issues.problem: 中文“一位在公司做设计的年轻人”没有性别，英文却写成“her parents”“support her”，给人物补上了中文没有的性别设定。
issues.proposed: 英文去掉性别，例如改为“a young in-house designer wants to convince their parents that going independent would pay the bills”；或在中文中同步说明性别。

verify.overall: 全文引语逐字可核，史实、时间线和解释标注基本到位；需要修正 dek 与 analysis.0 在传单归因上的矛盾，以及反思场景的中英性别不一致。另有一处措辞歧义建议顺手改掉。

issues.problem: 中文稿首次提到白璧德时只写“跟白璧德深造”，没有说明他是谁。到 story.4 才称他为“保守派批评家”。英文稿首次出现时已写明 the critic Irving Babbitt。

issues.problem: “梅光迪说的范围更宽”有歧义，读者容易理解为梅允许白话用的范围更宽。实际是他禁用的范围更大，连高级散文也包括在内。英文 drew the line more widely 有同样的问题。

evidence.quote: 但是在高级散文里——肯定的是在诗里面——白话千万用不得

issues.proposed: 中文改为“梅光迪划得更严：……”。英文改为“Mei drew the line more strictly: …”。

issues.problem: 稿件写“文章誊了三份”，后面只交代了两份去向，读者会以为漏写了第三份。

issues.problem: 末句“并非本文所据材料的记载 / not something recorded in the material this piece relies on”是在断言完整来源没有写什么，而证据包并不是全书。况且证据确实记载了陈独秀自己表述的“胡首举义旗、陈高张大旗作声援”的分工，这样写容易让读者误以为来源对此毫无记载。只需标明这是作者的推断即可。

issues.problem: 本段把“传单、送别诗、湖上险些翻船都是意外”写成胡适本人的史观。证据中胡适明确称作意外的是送别诗，并泛称“一连串的小意外事件”。写湖上划船一段时他说“虽然没有发生什么意外”，没有把这件事称作他所说的意外。把湖上险事（以及未被明确点名的传单）归入这一串，是本文自己的归并。英文同样有此问题。

inherited.rationale: 问题成立。胡适明确称送别诗为意外，写湖上一事时却说“没有发生什么意外”；把湖上险事归入他所说的意外，是本文的归并。已列为 F1，建议的措辞略有调整：传单在证据中也未被单独点名为意外。
